title: Military freezers become a suspected target
summary: Refrigeration failures affected at least six military commissaries and were investigated as a suspected cyberattack. NPR's November 3 review of public contracts found Danfoss controllers installed at some affected bases. Which equipment was compromised, the attack method, and any connection to Europe's attacks remain unconfirmed.

title: Supermarket fridges forced into defrost
summary: An overnight wave disrupted supermarket refrigeration and spoiled stock. France's CERT confirmed numerous compromises of Danfoss AK-SM and AK-SC controllers.

title: The attacks extend beyond Danfoss
summary: Further reporting described attacks on Dixell equipment. CERT-FR expanded its alert to include Copeland XWEB and Dixell XWEB controllers. This is a continuation of the October wave.

title: Another wave. More spoiled food.
summary: Refrigeration attacks were reported in Belgium, Estonia, Ireland, Luxembourg, the Netherlands and Sweden, with some settings raised to 50°C. Follow-up reports described contemporaneous incidents in Germany, Portugal and Sicily; connections between individual cases remain under investigation. Some affected systems used Danfoss controllers. A shared attacker across the waves remains unconfirmed. These reports do not establish a distinct new November 3 wave.

title: Blood-service cold storage is affected
summary: EFS confirmed that a refrigeration supplier incident altered cold-room temperature and defrost settings at three sites. Alarms enabled staff to secure equipment or transfer plasma; no product losses or health impact were reported, and collection and distribution continued. EFS did not identify the supplier or controller vendor. A link to the supermarket attacks remains unconfirmed.
